products.overview: Four wavelengths at full intensity, at once. The original managed one. Running multiple light wavelengths together used to mean turning the intensity down. PhotoCube Plus doesn't make that trade. It runs four wavelengths simultaneously, at full intensity, where the original PhotoCube could only manage one before intensity had to drop. Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm is usable, not a fixed set. An optional cooler module holds vials at 10–15°C at maximum LED power; without it, that same power runs at 40–50°C. The choice is real and it matters for reaction control. It's the first ThalesNano system built for both batch and flow. Four vials in batch mode, or an 8 mL loop in continuous flow, at 0.1 to 10 mL/min, on the same device.

faqs.question: What is the PhotoCube™ Plus used for?
faqs.answer: It's an LED photochemistry reactor used for reactions including bromination, C-C coupling, the Minisci reaction, and thiol-ene click chemistry, in both batch and continuous flow.

faqs.question: How many wavelengths can run at once?
faqs.answer: Up to four, at full intensity, a genuine improvement over the original PhotoCube's limit of one wavelength at high intensity.

faqs.question: How do I choose between batch and flow mode?
faqs.answer: Use batch mode with 4x4 mL or 4x30 mL vials for screening and method development, or flow mode with an 8 mL loop at 0.1 to 10 mL/min for continuous, scaled-up production.

faqs.question: How do I set up cooling for a temperature-sensitive reaction?
faqs.answer: Add the optional cooler module, which uses cold finger technology to hold vials at 10 to 15°C at maximum LED power, compared to 40 to 50°C without it.

faqs.question: What wavelength range is available?
faqs.answer: Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm, with a basic configuration of 365, 457, 523, and 625 nm, and custom wavelengths available on request.

faqs.question: Is the PhotoCube Plus safe to open while running?
faqs.answer: Yes. Opening the device door triggers an automatic lighting shutdown.

faqs.question: What pumps are compatible with the PhotoCube Plus?
faqs.answer: Knauer HPLC pumps (10 or 50 mL/min) and Eldex Optos HPLC pumps (up to 80 mL/min) are both confirmed compatible.

faqs.question: Can the PhotoCube Plus connect to ThalesNano's fleet system?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the THS System Controller and THS RS232-CAN Converter, using THS ReAction Software for remote and automated control.

faqs.question: What is the difference between PhotoCube Plus and the original PhotoCube?
faqs.answer: PhotoCube Plus runs four wavelengths at full intensity simultaneously versus the original's one, covers an open 257-650 nm range instead of a fixed set, and adds a proper cooler module and fleet compatibility the original didn't have.

faqs.question: What is the price of the PhotoCube™ Plus in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on whether you include the cooler module and any custom wavelength requirements. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your application is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the PhotoCube™ Plus in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano PhotoCube™ Plus in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.title: Wavelength Control and Cooling Performance
sections.tabSummary: What the cooler module actually changes
body: Running photochemistry at real intensity, across multiple wavelengths, generates real heat, and that's exactly what the cooler module is built to manage.

At maximum LED power, an uncooled vial sits at 40 to 50°C. With the cooler module's cold finger technology engaged, the same power holds the vial at 10 to 15°C, a genuinely different reaction environment for temperature-sensitive photochemistry. Wavelength control runs independently of that, with up to four wavelengths operable at once, at full intensity, across the open 257–650 nm range.
